assessments.reasoning: The License Index’s SCOPE.md at commit cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes relevant data. Its admission table, bytes [533,942), defines a license by an identifiable grant or licence text and edition supported by a controlling source. NLOD section 2 supplies that grant.

All four captures from https://data.norge.no/nlod/en/1.0 cover bytes [0,59381) contiguously and report the claimed whole-document SHA-256. The English title, Agency byline and “This version” link identify the witness. The preface identifies public-sector reuse, section 1 includes data sets, and section 2 grants copying, modification and distribution subject to the licence. Section 3 specifies exemptions. The Agency’s publication role is distinct from the responsible ministry’s role in issuing new versions under section 10.

The owning Index’s decision at commit afb962e68831a16accb80c70159b1e2f1fbb4dbc, bytes [2671,2890), names permanent ID e08b5a6060e143e8b48a93ad6bfd6b96, the opaque portion of the claim subject, with “Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 1.0”, edition nlod-1-0, revision sha256:cf9bbe13bb0fee9190be7002fa40c4095b42963678bf729c7011359d30f4940c, kind `license` and lifecycle `active`. The decision expressly limits the value to Index maintenance.

challenge.method: Tested whether the separate NLOD 2.0 row or the publisher’s latest-version landing page could stand in for the 1.0 witness, and whether the existence of 2.0 required a `historical` value for 1.0.
challenge.results: The English page identifies /nlod/en/1.0 as “This version” and gives a separate landing page for the latest publication. Section 10 permits a later-version choice subject to a licensor’s 1.0-only reservation. The Index gives 2.0 a different entity ID, edition and digest and explicitly marks both rows `active`. Neither the later edition nor the language discrepancy displaces the English 1.0 identity.

limitations: The documentary identity covers the English HTML. The Norwegian-language versioning discrepancy remains unresolved. The inspected English witness cannot establish equivalence between the language versions.
`active` means the Index maintains this reference for current lookup. Publisher currency and SPDX deprecation require separate evidence.

Application to a particular data set depends on the licensor making it available under the instrument and on the applicable terms and exemptions. Redistribution, installation eligibility and authorization to publish a consumer release require separate evidence.
reasoning: The Norwegian Digitalisation Agency’s English publication identifies NLOD 1.0 by title, edition and version-specific URL. Its operative grant covers information, including data sets. That grant satisfies the Index’s license criterion. The Index’s 2026-11-26 decision assigns `active` to the exact entity and publisher revision.
